# Welkom {.unnumbered}

Welcome to the **3XG Workshop**: a gentle introduction to statistical analysis based on the 3XG study.

## Over deze workshop

These notes are the companion material for a hands-on workshop that teaches the
basics of working with data in R. It is aimed at students interested in the 3XG study who want to learn how to explore, visualize, analyse and communicate about their data.

The workshop does not assume any prior programming experience. By the end
of it, you should be able to:

- Perform basic data wrangling and exploration.
- Create clear visualizations of your data.
- Organize your analysis in a reproducible way.

## How to work trough the course notes

These course notes are written with R Bookdown [@R-bookdown] in R Studio and rendered to an html file that is made available on GitHub. If you wish, you can convert the html to a pdf file. The best way to do this, is via the *print* function of your browser. Before doing so, you can best first collapse the sidebar (that contains the table of content).

Many **data analyses examples** are worked out in detail in the course notes, including the R code. When you access the course notes via GitHub, you can easily copy the R code and paste it to your local R software. Here is an example of a chunck of R code:
```{r}
### Simulate a normal distribution
#---------------------------------
Y <- rnorm(n = 100, mean = 0, sd = 1)
```
If you now move your mouse towards the upper right corner of the box that contains the R code, then you will see an icon appearing in that corner:

If you click on that icon, the content of the box will be copied to your clipboard so that you can paste it wherever you want (e.g. in a local R file). I actually advise that you also **work with your own local R script** to which you copy some of the R code of the course notes so that you can *play* with the data and the R code yourself.


## Why R?

R is a free, open-source programming language and environment designed
specifically for statistical computing and data analysis. It is widely
used across research institutes, including VITO, because it:

- Has a large ecosystem of packages for data wrangling, visualization,
  statistics, and reporting (many of them part of the
  [tidyverse](https://www.tidyverse.org/)).
- Makes reproducible analysis straightforward, which is essential for
  research studies like 3XG.
- Is free and works on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

## Tools you'll need

To follow along with this workshop, you'll need:

- **R** — download it from [CRAN](https://cran.r-project.org/).
- **RStudio** (or another R-friendly editor such as Positron or VS Code
  with the R extension) — download RStudio Desktop from
  [posit.co](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/).
